title: Biomarkers of critical illness neuromyopathy after intensive care therapy - Development of early detection methods through the integration of clinical, immunological, and muscular diagnostics
summary: The CritMyo study aims to identify biomarkers and early detection strategies for Critical-Illness-Neuromyopathy (CINM) in order to enable the early initiation of targeted therapy for affected patients. Following cardiac surgery, a substantial proportion of patients develop persistent physical, psychological, and/or cognitive impairments. These symptoms are collectively referred to as Post Intensive Care Syndrome (PICS). A major component of the physical impairment is the so-called intensive care unit acquired weakness (ICUAW), defined as an acquired skeletal muscle weakness occurring after necessary intensive care treatment. ICUAW may develop within the first days after admission to the intensive care unit and can lead to severe complications, including prolonged ventilator weaning or dysphagia. Furthermore, it may result in long-term impairment of patients’ quality of life. The underlying cause of ICUAW consists of pathological alterations affecting peripheral nerves and skeletal muscle, referred to as Critical-Illness-Neuromyopathy (CINM).

interventions.name: CINM risk group (N = 25): patients at risk of developing Critical-Illness-Neuromyopathy (CINM) following intensive care treatment (longer than 7 days)
Control group A (N = 25): patients with a short, uncomplicated intensive care unit (ICU) stay (discharge on postoperative day 1)
Control group B (N = 20): patients without ICU stay but with perioperative immobilization due to surgery of the lower extremity

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
requirement for intensive care treatment, voluntary participation, written informed consent following appropriate information, sufficient German language proficiency
Exclusion criteria:
inability to provide informed consent (due to linguistic, psychological or somatic reasons), employees involved in the conduct of the study, pre-existing or suspected polyneuropathy or myopathy, prior immobilization; secondary: withdrawal of consent, if applicable by a previously designated representative, contraindications to specific study procedures (e.g. anticoagulation)
